content:
Connor O'Brien: Heads up: we need to standardize PR labeling + release note capture across repos before we flip on the release-note preview check everywhere. Goal: consistent changelog generation for model metadata + promotions (public/internal split).

Connor O'Brien: Proposed label set (GitHub labels):
- `release-note:breaking`
- `release-note:security`
- `release-note:quality`
- `release-note:perf`
- `release-note:bugfix`
- `release-note:deprecation`
- `release-note:docs-only`
- `release-note:none`

Connor O'Brien: CI check behavior (draft): if PR touches `model-metadata/*.json` OR control plane emits model change events OR changelog templates => require exactly 1 of the above labels + a filled release note block in the PR description.

Sahana Iyer: +1. For the PR description block, can we keep it dead simple and enforce a marker? e.g.

```
## Release notes (required)
Public summary:
- 

Internal notes:
- 

Risk:
- Low | Medium | High

Rollout:
- Hosted | Dedicated | Private
```

Sahana Iyer: CI can parse between headers and fail if Public summary is empty (unless label is `release-note:none` or `docs-only`).

Michael Nguyen: For registry changes, we should be careful: a lot of the PRs are pure schema/invariants with no customer impact. `release-note:none` should be allowed but still generate an internal audit-only entry?

Connor O'Brien: Yeah, intent is:
- customer-visible artifacts generated only when label != `none`
- internal changelog/audit event always exists when metadata promoted (separate from PR)
PR labeling is mainly for release note templates + docs preview.

Chloe Martin: Can we avoid forcing labels on *all* PRs? It’s gonna be noisy for Console UI work. Maybe gate only when touching the known paths or when PR has `model-change` label?

Connor O'Brien: Agree. Scope triggers:
- `model-registry/**` JSON metadata + schema
- `control-plane/**` event emission / promotion workflow
- `changelog-generator/**` templates + category mapping
- `docs/**` release note generation pipeline
Everything else can ignore.

Dylan Brooks: For Console repo (`redwood`), we’ll hit this for endpoint work (release notes feed). That should probably be `release-note:bugfix` most of the time but no customer-facing model change. Are we OK with `release-note:none` there?

Wei Chen: From docs POV: if it’s Console UI only, I’d prefer `release-note:none` so it doesn’t show up on public model release notes pages. But we still might want Console product release notes later (separate taxonomy).

Connor O'Brien: Exactly. This is *model release notes* pipeline, not Console app release notes.

Elliot Price: We should document that explicitly, otherwise folks will assume “release note” label means “ship notes.”

Jordan Lee: Question: for policy engine changes that affect rollout eligibility (Hosted vs Dedicated rules), that’s customer-visible sometimes. Should those be captured here?

Connor O'Brien: If it changes how/when model versions get promoted (esp. eligibility constraints), yes. That’s typically `release-note:breaking` or `bugfix` depending. But we need guidance in the style guide for “behavioral change w/o model weights change.”

Quentin Harris: For model catalog entries: we already have `customer_impact` fields in some places. The new schema v1 has `visibility` and `notes.public` vs `notes.internal`. Can CI just validate those fields instead of PR text?

Sahana Iyer: Longer term maybe. Right now PR text is the quickest “human-reviewed” spot. CI will also validate metadata fields (schema) + redaction rules, but we still need a narrative summary for generated notes.

release-bot: Reminder: Repo rollout status (labels + CI) is tracked here: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-9826

Felix Schneider: For the preview artifact: can we get it posted as a PR comment w/ a permalink? Reviewers aren’t going to download random artifacts.

Sahana Iyer: Yup. Plan:
- CI uploads `release-note-preview.md` artifact
- `ci-bot` posts comment: “Preview” + link
- If PR is from fork, comment is skipped (security)

ci-bot: (example) Release note preview generated. Artifact: `release-note-preview.md` (expires in 30 days).

Dev Patel: Support ask: can we ensure `internal notes` are always present for model changes? Even if public summary is intentionally vague, we need something actionable.

Connor O'Brien: For any PR labeled `release-note:*` except `docs-only` / `none`, CI should require at least one bullet in Internal notes OR a `JIRA/SUP` link.

Chloe Martin: Redaction rule: internal notes should NEVER leak to public preview. We had a near-miss last month when a markdown include got rendered in docs build.

Wei Chen: +1 and please no account names in public summary. Style guide says “enterprise customer” not “Northbridge.”

Connor O'Brien: Proposed enforcement:
- Public summary: must not contain patterns like `@`, customer domains, or `SUP-`? (maybe too strict)
- Better: required “Public vs Internal” fields in metadata, and generator filters. But for PR text, we can just add lint warnings first.

Sahana Iyer: I can add a lightweight “redaction linter” in the CI job:
- hard fail if Public summary contains `internal-only:` or `SEV-` or `INC-`
- warn (not fail) if it contains `http` or looks like an email

Michael Nguyen: Rollout sequencing: can we do warn-only for a week? Otherwise all registry PRs will get blocked until everyone updates templates.

Connor O'Brien: Yes. Suggested timeline:
1) Today: add labels to org + publish guidance
2) Week 1: CI runs in warning mode (comment only)
3) Week 2: hard fail on missing label + missing Public summary when in-scope paths touched
4) Week 3: hard fail on redaction violations

Elliot Price: Docs team needs at least 1 week to update contributor docs and internal handbook. Also: can we provide copy-paste examples for each category? People struggle with “quality vs perf.”

Wei Chen: I’ll put together examples:
- perf: “Reduced median TTFT by ~12% on Hosted for typical chat workloads.”
- quality: “Adjusted default prompt formatting; improved instruction-following on internal eval set.” (w/ no numbers unless statistically significant)
- breaking: “Tokenizer change; pinned prompts may need updates. See migration guide.”

Jordan Lee: For “security”: we need a rule that public summary can be vague (“Hardened request validation”) and internal notes carry the full detail + incident references.

Connor O'Brien: Agree. For security, public summary required but can be minimal; internal notes required + security reviewer signoff.

Quentin Harris: Label mapping question: what if PR includes both perf + deprecation? For generator, we probably want multi-category.

Connor O'Brien: For now: exactly one label for simplicity. If multiple, pick the highest priority per taxonomy (breaking > security > deprecation > quality > perf > bugfix > docs-only). We can revisit multi-label once templates support sections.

Chloe Martin: Who’s updating the repos?
- redwood-model-registry: Quentin/Michael
- redwood control plane: Ethan’s team (I can nudge)
- docs: Elliot/Wei
- SDKs: probably DevEx but might not be in scope right away

Connor O'Brien: I’ll own org label creation + the shared “Release note preview” GitHub Action in `.github`.
Sahana will own CI parsing + PR comment bot.
Quentin/Michael will dogfood in model registry and adjust based on pain.

Sahana Iyer: Can we add a single-source doc for engineers? Confluence is fine but I’d like a `RELEASENOTES.md` in each repo too.

Connor O'Brien: +1. I’ll add a short `docs/release-notes/README.md` template and we can copy into repos.

Dev Patel: One more request: include “Roll back” guidance when label is breaking/high risk. Even a link to the rollback runbook.

Connor O'Brien: Good call. We can make “Risk: High” require a Rollback bullet or link.

Connor O'Brien: Action items:
- [Connor] Create org labels + announce in #eng (today)
- [Sahana] Land CI preview job in model registry (warn-only) (by EOW)
- [Wei/Elliot] Examples + category guidance (early next week)
- [Quentin/Michael] Dogfood + report edge cases (ongoing)
